scope: Disposable local SQLite data only. Subjects are supplied fixture users, assumed authenticated upstream; no real credentials or network.
threat_model: Synthetic private note bodies are protected assets. Actor can manipulate username/note_id or choose another owner. SQL and object ownership are the relevant boundaries.

findings.path: Raw input concatenated into SQL reveals both owners; parameterized owner/id query now rejects payload as data.
Delete ignores supplied owner; now owner and id are matched in the data query with rowcount result.
Hardcoded synthetic secret removed; get_secret reads NOTES_SECRET and rejects missing/empty config.

verification: 5 tests; before 4 failures; after all pass.
limitations: Authentication is a caller precondition; this fixture has no HTTP boundary.
Environment secrecy/storage and real credential rotation were not tested.
Synthetic seed credential value redacted in retained diff.
